title: Comparison of one saturated log blowup with normalization
statement:
Let $(X,M)$ be a log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] with $X$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $\mathcal I\subset M$ be a nonempty coherent log ideal, and put $J=\alpha(\mathcal I)\mathcal O_X$. Then $J$ is a nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, and the saturated log blowup $b:(X',M')\to(X,M)$ exists and is log regular. Its underlying scheme morphism is canonically isomorphic over $X$ to
$$\bigl(\operatorname{Bl}_J X\bigr)^\nu\longrightarrow\operatorname{Bl}_J X\longrightarrow X,$$
where the superscript $\nu$ means normalization in the function field [def-sc-normalization], and the ordinary blowup is locally the scheme covered, for a finite set of ideal generators $a$, by $\operatorname{Spec}A[J/a]$ with $A[J/a]\subset A_a$ the subalgebra generated by $j/a$, $j\in J$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring, prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover]. If $U$ is the triviality locus of $(X,M)$, then $b^{-1}U\to U$ is an isomorphism and the triviality locus of $(X',M')$ is exactly $b^{-1}U$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.4.1--3.4.6(i), printed pp. 110--111 (monoidal ideals and normalized-blowup comparison); 3.3.8--3.3.11, printed pp. 107--108, and Expose VI, 1.8, printed p. 70 (log regularity preserved). The triviality-locus assertion is the universal property over U and the local homomorphism on local rings outside U.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction], $J$ is finite type and quasi-coherent. By [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure], $U$ is open dense and every local log section restricts to a unit on $U$. Hence the nonempty ideal $\mathcal I$ gives $J|_U=\mathcal O_U$, so $J\ne0$. On any nonempty affine open of integral $X$, a monomial chart generator is nonzero wherever that chart is nonempty: it is invertible on its intersection with the dense $U$. This also rules out a zero denominator in the nonempty blowup charts below.

Apply [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction] to construct the fine unsaturated log blowup $(X_0,M_0)$ and the fs log scheme $(X',M')$, with a finite map $s:X'\to X_0$. The fs universal property is exactly the saturated log blowup of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. In a strict etale chart of $X$, write $E=\{h_1,\ldots,h_r\}$, $H=E+P$, and $Q_h=P[H-h]$. Its saturated charts have rings $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_h^{\mathrm{sat}}]$. The saturated monoids are finitely generated by the chart-construction input and have the same group completion as $P$. Therefore [lem-trf-log-regular-toric-refinement] makes these charts log regular and locally Noetherian. These are etale-local conditions (the definition checks geometric strict local rings), so $(X',M')$ is log regular and locally Noetherian.

We identify the unsaturated chart with an ordinary blowup chart, rather than assuming that arbitrary blowups commute with nonflat base change. Set $L=\mathbf Z[H]\subset\mathbf Z[P]$, $J_A=(\alpha(h):h\in H)$. For every $n\geq0$, apply [lem-trf-log-regular-monomial-tor] to the monoid ideal $nH$ (with $0H=P$). It identifies $A\otimes\mathbf Z[nH]$ with $J_A^n$. The maps send $a\otimes z^p$ to $a\alpha(p)$; hence they preserve multiplication, since $\alpha(p+q)=\alpha(p)\alpha(q)$. They thus identify the base-changed graded ring $A\otimes\bigoplus_{n\geq0}L^nt^n$ with $\bigoplus_{n\geq0}J_A^nt^n$. Inverting $z^ht$ and taking degree zero expresses the first ring as the colimit of $A\otimes L^n$, with transition multiplication by $z^h$. Its elements are the fractions represented by $a\otimes z^{p-nh}$; their addition, multiplication and transition relations are precisely those of $A\otimes\mathbf Z[Q_h]$. On the second side the fractions are $j/\alpha(h)^n$ with $j\in J_A^n$, so the result is $A[J_A/\alpha(h)]$ as in [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. These maps agree on the overlaps of the charts of one $\operatorname{Spec}A$, because further localization uses the very same fractions. With the affine cover of [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover], they identify $X_0\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A$, which is the fine log blowup of the chart by the strict-etale compatibility in [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction], with $\operatorname{Bl}_{J_A}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Steps 4--5 globalize this to $B=\operatorname{Bl}_JX$.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.4.3, and proof of 3.4.6 (monomial Rees algebra calculation).

proof.text: Fix a family of strict etale charts $g_i:\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to X$ as in Step 3 covering $X$. Each $g_i$ is etale, hence flat, so [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] says that $\operatorname{bc}_{g_i}:\operatorname{Bl}_{J_{A_i}}(\operatorname{Spec}A_i)\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i\times_XB$ [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] is an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$; here $J\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A_i}=J_{A_i}$ by [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction]. Composing with Step 3 gives isomorphisms $\tilde\varphi_i:X_0\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to B\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$; put $\varphi_i=\mathrm{pr}_B\circ\tilde\varphi_i$, an $X$-morphism. Invertibility: on the chart $\operatorname{Spec}A_i[J_{A_i}/\alpha(h)]$ the extended ideal of $J$ is generated by $\alpha(h)$. By [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure] applied to the log regular chart $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, $\alpha(h)$ is a unit on a dense open of a scheme whose local rings are domains, so it is a non-zero-divisor of $A_i$, hence of $A_i[J_{A_i}/\alpha(h)]\subset(A_i)_{\alpha(h)}$. Tensoring the injection given by multiplication by $\alpha(h)$ with a flat algebra keeps it injective. So for every $T$ flat over $X_0\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, in particular $T=X_0\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A_i\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A_j$, the extended ideal $J\mathcal O_T$ is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor, hence invertible. On that $T$ the two $X$-morphisms $\varphi_i\circ p_1$ and $\varphi_j\circ p_2$ to $B$ therefore coincide, by the uniqueness clause of [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property].

source.place: VIII proof of 3.4.6 ('All claims can be checked etale locally'); Stacks 0805 (divisors.tex, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up) and 0806 (divisors.tex, lemma-universal-property-blowing-up).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale] the family $(g_i)$ is an fpqc covering of $X$, and by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms] its base changes $(X_0\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to X_0)$ and $(B\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to B)$ are fpqc coverings. By Step 4 the morphisms $\varphi_i$ agree on the fibre products, so [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] gives a unique $\varphi:X_0\to B$ with $\varphi\circ p_i=\varphi_i$; it lies over $X$ because both composites to $X$ agree after the covering, by the uniqueness in the same lemma. The base change of $\varphi$ along $g_i$ is $\tilde\varphi_i$, an isomorphism. The morphisms $\psi_i=\mathrm{pr}_{X_0}\circ\tilde\varphi_i^{-1}:B\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to X_0$ agree on $B\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A_i\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A_j$, where both are the projection composed with the inverse of the base change of $\varphi$ to that fibre product. Descent gives $\psi:B\to X_0$. Both $\psi\varphi$ and $\mathrm{id}_{X_0}$ restrict to the projections on the covering of $X_0$, and $\varphi\psi$ and $\mathrm{id}_B$ on the covering of $B$, so uniqueness of descent makes $\varphi$ an isomorphism over $X$, $X_0\cong B$. It is canonical, being the unique morphism compatible with the canonical chart isomorphisms $\tilde\varphi_i$.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.4.6 (etale-local reduction); Stacks 022C (topologies.tex) and 023Q (descent.tex, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms) for descent of morphisms.

proof.text: Over $U$, every element of $M$ is a unit. Thus $\mathcal I|_U=M|_U$, an ideal generated by the identity. The identity of $U$ has the fs universal property, so [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] identifies the restriction $b^{-1}U\to U$ with the identity as a log scheme. In particular its log structure is trivial. Conversely take a geometric point $x'\in X'$ with image $x\notin U$. There exists $m\in M_{\bar x}$ with nonunit structural image in $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$; otherwise the defining inverse-image-of-units condition of a log structure would make its characteristic zero. The induced homomorphism of strict local rings is local, so the image of $\alpha(m)$ is in the maximal ideal at $x'$. Its corresponding log section in $M'_{\bar x'}$ is therefore not a unit, by the same condition. Thus $x'$ is outside the triviality locus. This proves that the triviality locus of $M'$ is exactly $b^{-1}U$.

The ordinary blowup $B$ is integral, with function field $k(X)$. Indeed, on any integral affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, the nonempty charts supplied by [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] have rings $A[J/a]\subset A_a\subset\operatorname{Frac}A$ by [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], with $a\ne0$. They are domains with fraction field $\operatorname{Frac}A$ and contain the same generic point. This generic point is dense in each chart and the charts glue with it, hence $B$ is irreducible and reduced. The generic points agree on intersecting affine opens of integral $X$. No finiteness of normalization is being assumed here.

source.place: VIII 3.4.6(i), ordinary blowup charts; elementary integrality argument, also Stacks 02ND (divisors.tex, lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure] to the log regular fs scheme of Step 2. It makes $X'$ normal and its triviality locus dense. By Step 6 that locus is $b^{-1}U\cong U$, which is nonempty and irreducible because it is a dense open in integral $X$. Its closure is therefore irreducible; normality implies reducedness, so $X'$ is integral. By Steps 2--5 the map $s:X'\to B$ is finite. It is closed, and its image contains the dense open $U$, so it is surjective; hence every nonempty affine open of $B$ has nonempty inverse image. It is the identity on the common dense open $U$, so its two function fields are canonically $k(X)$. For an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset B$, its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}D$ for a finite $C$-algebra $D$. These are domains inside $k(X)$ and $D$ is integrally closed there, by the cited normality statement. Thus $D$ equals the integral closure of $C$: each element of $D$ is integral over $C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]; and an element of $k(X)$ integral over $C$ is also integral over $D$ and hence belongs to $D$. By [def-sc-normalization] these are exactly the normalization rings. Their inclusions in the common field agree on all overlaps, giving the canonical identification $X'\cong B^\nu$ over $B$ and hence over $X$.

source.place: VIII 3.4.6(i), saturated comparison; VI 1.4 and VIII 3.5 for normality. Integral-closure identification spelled out.

tool_uses.why: Generic affine cover of ordinary blowups used in the chart comparison and integrality argument; it does not replace any step of the logarithmic route.
Step 4: blowups commute with the flat strict etale chart maps (Stacks 0805); generic blowup fact, no node of sk-i-curve-zero states it.

lean.note: The monoidal ideal is existentially specified by equality of its extensions to every geometric stalk with the span of structural images of the log ideal. This characterizes the actual ideal α(I) O_X, including étale-only local generators; no object is selected from an existence proof. The integral-blowup witness supplies the instance required by Scheme.normalization. The open U is the triviality locus, and the normalization comparison is unique over X.
